most_common: Community Board 1 approved the plan amendment 35-5 but raised a substantive concern about replacing 42 percent of planned park space, and its District Manager asked CPC to delay until the board completed review of Site 4C. Parks said it would seek to develop Site 7, but that response remained contingent on funding and priorities; CPC approved the amendment despite the unresolved certainty of replacement open space.

Community Board 10 approved 39-2 with conditions requiring an R5B underlying district to prevent future out-of-scale development and remediation of former gas-station contamination. CPC explicitly found both requests addressed through the Dyker Heights Rezoning and the binding Conditional Negative Declaration. CPC approved the commercial overlay for the bank, with no hearing opposition or unresolved local objection.

Community Board 10 supported the rezoning and no local opposition or condition was documented. CPC raised concerns about soft sites, visual effects, streetwall and bulk, and pressure on the Apollo and Loews theaters; the applicant signed a restrictive declaration limiting streetwall height and FAR, and CPC approved with no unresolved local objection.

Community Board 11 and the Borough President approved the nursing-home enlargement without conditions, and no one spoke at the joint CPC hearing. Review addressed the sixth-floor addition’s scale, traffic, and expanded resident services, but documented no local request, opposition, concession, or unresolved objection.

Community Board 12 approved only six parcels, and America Sevashram Sangha opposed unrestricted disposition of the seventh parcel because it used the lot for scarce parking and planned a pre-kindergarten program. The Borough President requested accessory-use restrictions on four parcels; CPC adopted the restrictions for three small lots. CPC rejected the requested community-facility restriction for Block 9755 Lot 59 and approved its disposition pursuant to zoning, leaving that local objection unresolved.
